assumptions: ELM's class regular expressions and filters as bundled.
limits: A regex match is a candidate, not an annotated instance.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which short linear motifs from ELM does this protein carry, after ELM's own filters?

description: Short linear motifs in a protein: degrons, docking sites, targeting signals, cleavage and modification sites — the three-to-eleven-residue functional sites a profile-HMM domain scan cannot see. Runs ELM's own class patterns ON THIS MACHINE; only the class table is fetched. Applies ELM's context filters: the chance-probability cutoff, family selection, and the globular-domain filter when you pass domains. It does NOT scan for DOMAINS — for those call scan_protein_domains, which submits to EMBL-EBI InterProScan and returns `domains` in exactly the form this tool's `domains` parameter takes.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

compartments.description: restrict to motifs whose class is annotated for these cell compartments, as GO ids, comma-separated (e.g. GO:0005634 for nucleus). Empty runs no compartment filter, which is ELM's own default.

domains.description: the globular domains to bury motifs in, as `start-end` residue ranges (1-based, inclusive), comma-separated, each optionally labeled `start-end@label` so a dropped hit can say what buried it — e.g. `20-153@G3DSA:3.90.180.10, 296-341@G3DSA:3.90.180.10`. Pass the FRAGMENTS of an InterProScan domain match, not its outer span. Empty falls back to the scan the Protein domains panel holds, which is the only source the in-browser doors need. Only applies when filterInDomains is true.

expectCutoff.description: ELM's class gate: classes whose chance probability per residue exceeds this are not scanned at all. ELM's own default is 0.01; 0 scans every class, which is the resource's “all found (before filtering)” listing.

families.description: restrict to these ELM families, comma-separated, from CLV, DEG, DOC, LIG, MOD, TRG. Empty is no restriction and scans every family; the literal "none" is a restriction to no family and scans nothing, which is what the panel does when every family is unticked.

filterInDomains.description: apply ELM's globular-domain filter, dropping motifs buried inside a folded domain. Takes the domains from `domains` when you pass them, and otherwise from the scan the Protein domains panel currently holds; with neither, the call refuses rather than silently not filtering.

protein.description: the protein sequence, one-letter codes; wire it from translate_sequence or read it off a CDS.

species.description: the species the protein comes from, as an NCBI Taxonomy id (e.g. 4932) or a scientific name (e.g. Saccharomyces cerevisiae), for ELM's taxonomic range filter: a motif whose class ELM does not place in that species' lineage is dropped, with its range. Empty runs no taxon filter, which is ELM's own default.

structuralContext.description: score each motif's structural context, as ELM's structure filter does. Empty applies nothing, which is the panel's own default. `alphafold` uses the predicted model and yields Q_acc only. A four-character PDB id (e.g. `1crn`) uses that experimental entry and yields Q_acc, Q_sse and ELM's three-way verdict, because only a real entry has a DSSP file. Either way the protein is resolved to its UniProt entry by sequence checksum first, and the call refuses if it is not an exact match.

name: find_linear_motifs

accounting.description: what the scan was actually run against — classes scanned, classes skipped by the cutoff, classes skipped by the family selection — so a hit count can be read against its denominator rather than on its own

count.description: surviving motifs, after every filter that ran

hits.description: each surviving motif, in the engine’s own field names: identifier, accession, functionalSiteName, description, 1-based start/end, the residues that matched, the class chance probability, and how many experimentally annotated instances ELM holds

provenance.description: the ELM release and date the scan ran against, and the filters that ran
